title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 230 (Power to compromise or make arrangements with creditors and members)

content.overview: Section 230 empowers the Tribunal, on application by the company, any creditor or member, or the liquidator (if the company is being wound up), to order a meeting of creditors or class of creditors, or of members or class of members, and to sanction a compromise or arrangement if approved by a majority of persons representing three-fourths in value of the creditors or members voting, and if the Tribunal is satisfied as to fairness and statutory compliance. The notice must disclose the effect on creditors, members, promoters and directors and any material interest. Persons holding not less than 5% of the shareholding or 5% of the outstanding debt may object. The sanctioned order binds and is filed with the Registrar. Listed companies also face SEBI and exchange conditions, which are additional, not a replacement of s. 230.
content.glance: Tribunal may order meeting and sanction compromise/arrangement: majority in number representing 3/4 in value; disclosure of effect and interests; 5% objection threshold; order binds on filing; SEBI conditions additional for listed cos.
content.study: Where a compromise or arrangement is proposed between a company and its creditors or any class of them, or between the company and its members or any class of them, an application may be made to the Tribunal by the company, any creditor or member, or the liquidator. The Tribunal may order a meeting. The compromise or arrangement shall be binding if agreed to by a majority of persons representing three-fourths in value of the creditors or members (or class) present and voting, and if sanctioned by the Tribunal. Current-law framing: identify applicant; obtain meeting order; ensure notice discloses effects and material interests; achieve majority + three-fourths in value; address objections by 5% holders; Tribunal sanction on fairness and legality; file order with Registrar. Distinct from merger/amalgamation under s. 232 and fast-track under s. 233.

sections.heading: Application and Meeting
sections.body: Application by company, creditor, member, or liquidator; Tribunal may order meeting of creditors or members (or class).

sections.heading: Disclosure
sections.body: Notice must disclose effect on creditors, members, promoters and directors, and any material interest of directors/promoters/managers.

sections.heading: Majority
sections.body: Majority of persons representing three-fourths in value of creditors or members (or class) present and voting.

sections.heading: Objection and Sanction
sections.body: Objection by persons holding not less than 5% shareholding or 5% outstanding debt; Tribunal sanctions if statutory compliance and fairness satisfied; order binds on filing with Registrar.

provisions.title: Power to compromise or make arrangements with creditors and members

examples.title: Value test
examples.body: A scheme is approved by a headcount majority of creditors but they represent only half the value of debt voting. Section 230 requires majority of persons representing three-fourths in value — the value test fails.

examples.title: Disclosure of director interest
examples.body: A scheme notice omits that a director has a substantial interest in the counterparty. Section 230 requires disclosure of material interests; defective disclosure can defeat sanction.

hypotheticals.question: Is a simple majority of members enough to approve a s. 230 scheme?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The statute requires a majority of persons representing three-fourths in value of those voting in the class. Headcount alone is not enough.

distinctions.title: Compromise/arrangement (s. 230) vs merger/amalgamation (s. 232)
distinctions.left: General power to compromise or arrange with creditors or members
distinctions.right: Additional requirements where the scheme is a merger or amalgamation (valuation, RD/OL reports, dissolution without winding up)

misconceptions.trap: The Tribunal rewrites the commercial terms of a scheme if it disagrees with the majority.
misconceptions.correction: The Tribunal checks statutory compliance, class fairness, informed approval and absence of illegality. It does not substitute its own commercial bargain for the statutory majority (Miheer Mafatlal principle).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 230 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify applicant and class. II. Meeting and disclosure. III. Majority + 3/4 value. IV. Objections and Tribunal sanction. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Scheme terms; class composition; voting; disclosure; fairness; precise relief.

examTips: Tribunal: legality and fairness, not commercial rewrite.
SEBI conditions additional for listed cos.

enhancement.definition: Section 230 allows the Tribunal to order a meeting and sanction a compromise or arrangement with creditors or members if approved by a majority representing three-fourths in value and if fairness and statutory compliance are satisfied.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Creditor and member compromises bind the class when the statutory majority approves and the Tribunal is satisfied that the scheme is fair and lawful.
essentialIngredients: Disclosure of effects and material interests
Tribunal sanction; order filed with Registrar
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 230 is the primary compromise and arrangement power under Chapter XV.
